question: The component of white light that deviates the most on passing through a glass prism is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**violet**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Violet** light **deviates the most** when passing through a glass prism.
 
• This is due to the fact that violet light has the **shortest wavelength **of all the colors in visible light, and shorter wavelengths are refracted more than longer wavelengths.
 
• The phenomenon of light splitting into its constituent colors is called **dispersion**, and it occurs because different wavelengths of light are refracted by different amounts.
 
• The order of colors from least to most deviation through a prism is red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, and violet (often remembered by the acronym **ROYGBIV**).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Isaac Newton** was the first to demonstrate that white light is made up of a spectrum of colors by using a glass prism.
 
• When white light enters a prism, it slows down and bends. Each color bends by a different amount because each color travels at a different speed in the glass.
 
• This separation of light into different colors is what produces the **spectrum**.
 
• In natural phenomena, dispersion is responsible for the formation of **rainbows**, where sunlight is dispersed by water droplets in the atmosphere.
